notes: Stage A: None. The prompt names a place and a mood, no game type; no-genre.md loaded, no genre file.
Preset Explorable Place taken whole. Every axis left at its default, so the route is P0.
'3d' read as the ordinary build medium, not as a request for volumetric play-space; axis-play-space left at grounded-surface, no CHECK.

No terrain-relief applied. The prompt says 'desert' but names no dunes, mesas, canyon or cliffs, and universal options are not to be taken unasked — so the map is a single-surface exterior and stays off P0 + tiered. Reversible if the user says the ground has landform.

Scale band 'district' assumed: the prompt names neither an extent nor anything that lives in the space, so the assumption was made from the preset's landmark and circulation paths rather than from the prompt.

skill_gap.name: no biome or ground-cover option
skill_gap.why: the entire prompt is a biome, and nothing in no-genre.md's table, the universal six, or the shape axes carries what the ground is made of. terrain-relief covers landform, not surface material, so 'desert' survived only as free-text theme — which layout-intake defines as set dressing that never changes the route.

notes_for_us: no-genre.md has no option for biome or ground material; 'desert' is the whole prompt and lands only in free-text theme.

layout-intake says ask about scale only when the prompt names an extent without naming what lives in it. It gives no rule for a prompt naming neither, which is this one, so the band was assumed with no guidance.
Universal options are explicitly never defaults, so terrain-relief was withheld from a desert prompt where dunes are arguably the map. The rule and the obvious build disagree here.
The theme table's Post-Apocalyptic reads as 'overgrown foliage, rusted metal' — wrong vocabulary for an arid wasteland, so theme had to be written free-text against the table.
prompts.json carries no `enriched` field, so coverage.enriched_invented could not be filled as LANE-BRIEF describes.
